If nobody else ever knew what you chose, would your decision change?

It's worth asking when you're weighing a new job, a move, or a personal project. Sometimes we're considering more than our own needs and responsibilities. We're also imagining how the choice will look to everyone else.

Decision Untangler helps you explore the influences behind a difficult choice: https://decisionuntangler.garrettsdevdesk.com

Other people can influence your decisions without ever saying a word.

You start imagining how you'll explain your choice, whether it sounds impressive, or whether someone will think you're making a mistake. Before long, those imagined reactions become another factor to weigh.

Try writing down whose opinions you're considering. Then ask which concerns come from actual conversations and which ones you've supplied yourself.

There's a difference between considering how your choice affects someone and worrying about how they'll judge you.

A family's financial needs, a partner's priorities, or an existing commitment may deserve real weight. Imagined opinions about whether your decision looks impressive deserve a different kind of scrutiny.

Explore those competing considerations with Decision Untangler: https://decisionuntangler.garrettsdevdesk.com

Try imagining your next big decision without the announcement that comes afterward.

There's no LinkedIn post, no group chat update, and no explanation over dinner. You simply make the choice, wake up tomorrow, and begin living with it.

Which option feels different when you picture the ordinary life that follows instead of the moment you tell everyone about it?

A decision can be easy to explain to other people and still lead to a life you don't particularly want.

The impressive job title, exciting move, or ambitious project may come with tradeoffs that matter more to you than the public recognition. A quieter choice can be just as thoughtful.

Decision Untangler helps you consider what fits your priorities rather than simply what looks good from the outside: https://decisionuntangler.garrettsdevdesk.com

Sometimes a useful decision-making exercise is to ask the imaginary audience to step outside for a moment.

Keep the needs of people who are genuinely affected by your choice in view. Then set aside the reactions you've only imagined and listen to what matters to you.

Have you ever realized that you were leaning toward an option mainly because it would be easier to explain to other people?
